text:
riley: Heads up — PR 3167 caused a formatter exception on Windows CI, failing gofmt checks for some generated clients. pinging for a quick decision; @anita can you confirm whether the rename is intentional? CI: https://ci.example.com/build/12345 :grimacing:
anita: On it. I glanced at the logs — looks like a `gofumpt` vs `gofmt` discrepancy. Can you paste the small diff or the `gofmt -s` output?
riley: Sure, here's the minimal diff from the generator that triggered it:
```diff
- func GetUserID(ctx context.Context) string {
+ func GetUserId(ctx context.Context) string {
 }
```
This came from a codegen template tweak earlier today.
ken: We should keep the initialism as `ID` (GetUserID). That rename will ripple through a few call sites. Seems like the generator applied gofumpt rules. I'd prefer reverting the rename in the generator and reformatting.
format-bot: format-bot: automated note — I reformatted files in PR 3167 using gofumpt. Recommend running `gofumpt -w .` locally before pushing new commits.
anita: Two options: (1) tiny revert PR to restore `ID` and run `gofumpt` consistently, or (2) add a generated-file header exception and leave the rename. I vote for (1) to avoid special-casing codegen.
sam: +1 for revert. Small PR, low blast radius.
riley: I'll open a revert PR that also runs `gofumpt -w` and includes CI green check. Will link shortly.
riley: PR posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/3210 — @ken can you give a quick LGTM? CI should be green after the formatter pass.
ken: Looking now, will review in ~20. If it's the simple rename revert + fmt, I'll approve. :thumbsup:
format-bot: format-bot: CI note — once PR 3210 merges, please rebase any open branches against main to pick up the restored names.
riley: Thanks all — will merge after ken approves and CI passes.
